newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, EU work for deal on vexed issues.
newsitem.headline: Poland, EU work for deal on vexed issues.

text.p: European Commissioner Hans van den Broek urged Poland on Thursday to speed up its preparations for EU membership, while behind the scenes experts worked to solve disagreements on oil, steel and other trade issues.
"We have very much encouraged the government to accelerate the pace of preparations," he told reporters in Warsaw after talks with Polish officials and President Aleksander Kwasniewski.
"The commission will come next year with its opinion of the applications and shortly therefter the decision about the opening of the official negotiations," he said.
Earlier this year the Commission strongly criticised Poland, which hopes to join the EU by the year 2000, over its plans to extend a protection period for its steel and oil industries.
The Polish industry ministry has proposed beginning to phase out customs duties on oil and steel products in 1999 instead of 1997 as originally agreed with the EU.
Western diplomats said a central purpose of Van den Broek's visit was to sort out differences on these and other issues, including recognition of EU countries' safety certificates.
Polish Deputy Industry Minister Danuta Hubner said the talks were making progress but would last late into the evening and on into Friday.
"We are in the stage of approaching agreement. This is a working visit. Concessions will be required on both sides," she told reporters.

Van den Broek signed an agreement with Poland under the EU's PHARE aid programme, releasing a 65 million Ecu tranche to be used for improving transport infrastructure, helping Polish privatisation and promoting exports by small and medium-sized firms.
This is part of total PHARE grants amounting to more than one billion Ecu over the 1995 to 1999 period being made available to Poland to help it adjust for future EU membership.
Despite strains evident during the visit, van den Broek was encouraging for Poland's aspirations.

"We said again that not only does the EU consider Poland an important partner but we also feel that this is a country with great potential of being the front-runner in the accession negotiations," Van den Broek, responsible for relations with Central and Eastern Europe, told reporters.
On Friday he was due to meet Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz before winding up the two-day trip.
